readboj: Auditable Access to Bank of Japan Statistics

Source: R/readboj-package.R
readboj-package.Rd

readboj retrieves official Bank of Japan statistical responses while preserving the exact source identity needed for reproducible analysis. It normalizes observations and metadata into stable data frames, retains raw response and semantic hashes, and exposes source, cache, parser, and API details through boj_provenance().

Supported surfaces

The package supports the Bank of Japan Time-Series Data Search API through read_boj_series(), read_boj_layer(), boj_metadata(), and search_boj_series(). boj_databases() provides the locally pinned bilingual database registry. read_boj_snapshot() parses a local API response for deterministic offline workflows.

Selected official flat/bulk files can be discovered with list_boj_bulk_files(), downloaded with download_boj_bulk(), and read with read_boj_bulk(). Dated Tankan comprehensive-data release pages and their XLS, XLSX, and ZIP assets are exposed by list_boj_tankan_releases(), list_boj_tankan_assets(), download_boj_tankan_asset(), and read_boj_workbook(). A portable metadata catalogue can be built and searched with build_boj_catalogue_snapshot() and search_boj_catalogue_snapshot().

Published Outlook forecasts use list_boj_outlook_releases() and read_boj_outlook() for saved local reads, with update_boj_outlook() and maintain_boj_outlook() as separate source/calendar maintenance routes. The complete bundled Outlook history is official-source numeric data, unlike the small synthetic parser fixtures. See the individual help topics.

Output and provenance

Observation and metadata readers return ordinary data frames with stable names, explicit date/value columns, and source identity in a readboj_provenance attribute. JSON nulls and API CSV blank cells remain distinguishable through the documented raw/status columns; bulk NA/ND markers remain literal text. Bulk and workbook readers preserve text values and workbook/archive structure rather than guessing a time-series model. Use boj_provenance() to inspect provenance; it does not revalidate a moved file or an external URL.

Network, cache, and filesystem behavior

Live operations use HTTPS and an allowlist of official Bank of Japan hosts. They use bounded timeouts, retries, response sizes, pagination, archive sizes, and result sizes. There are no startup downloads and no credential prompts. Request snapshots are stored under tools::R_user_dir("readboj", "cache") by default, or under the caller's cache_dir/option. Cache objects are content-addressed, success-only, and bounded by package options; use boj_cache_prune() for explicit local maintenance. The package writes only caller-selected output directories, its managed cache, and temporary files under tempdir. Set offline = TRUE on reader functions that support it to require cached snapshots and avoid network access.

Limits and failure modes

Safety bounds are intentional. Defaults include 30- or 60-second API timeouts, depending on the operation, bounded retries, 128 MiB response limits, 2 GiB/1,000-object cache limits, pagination and cell/row limits, and bounded bulk/workbook archive limits. The large Tankan CO metadata catalogue is not eagerly materialised unless explicitly allowed; use search_boj_series() for discovery. Invalid parameters, changed official schemas, unsafe paths, validated cache corruption, identity mismatches, offline misses, rate limits, authorization failures, transport failures, and size/deadline violations raise typed readboj conditions. These checks are fail-closed; callers should handle availability and upstream schema changes explicitly. Unexpected base or dependency errors from manually malformed local metadata or third-party files should be reported with their input identity.

Official sources and terms

The upstream service is the Bank of Japan Time-Series Data Search. The package's API credit and current notice/copyright links are returned by boj_api_credit(). BOJ terms remain applicable to live responses and downloaded materials; readboj does not grant permission to redistribute them. Bundled extdata includes small synthetic fixtures for deterministic tests and examples, plus the separately identified saved Outlook history. Outlook publication/graphic rights and commercial reuse restrictions remain with BOJ; this package does not establish permission to redistribute that material. Package code is MIT licensed, copyright Chartwell Macro. That package licence does not reassign rights in Bank of Japan data, publications, services, or other upstream material. The package retains the required third-party attribution in inst/NOTICE/bojapi-MIT.txt.
